key_insight: LizTail unifies shape adaptation and spatial parallelism by splitting a 128×128 systolic array into reconfigurable 128×4 segments, letting the hardware both fit awkward matrix shapes and execute independent sub-tasks efficiently.
engineering_relevance: This matters for AI accelerators because CNNs and especially autoregressive LLM decoding often leave fixed arrays underutilized, so segment-level reconfiguration can raise PE utilization without the cost of full PE-level routing.
method: Partitions the array into 32 regular segments with connectivity only at predefined endpoints.
Supports trimming, 180° turn-back extension, and distributed execution across subarrays.
Uses differentiated PE datapaths plus segment-aware CEB/SIB buffers, with a hardware-constrained mapper choosing execution mode and tiling.
evidence_signal: On representative workloads, the design reports geometric-mean speedups of 5.02× for CNN inference and 25.67× for LLM decoding versus a TPU-like array, with EDP reductions up to 38.23×.
watch_item: The added flexibility still depends on constrained predefined boundaries and custom mapping, so real performance may be sensitive to compiler quality, workload fit, and hardware implementation overheads.
paper_title: LizTail: Unifying Shape Adaptation and Spatial Parallelism with Segment-Reconfigurable Systolic Arrays
